filename: Data-driven dimensionality reduction and causal inference for spatiotemporal climate fields.pdf
title: Data-driven dimensionality reduction and causal inference for spatiotemporal climate fields
ml_methods: Graph inference with distance-constrained adjacency matrix
Analytical null model for fluctuation-response inference
testbed_rationale: The paper focuses on data-driven dimensionality reduction and linear-response-based causal inference diagnostics for large-scale SST variability, not on developing parameterization or emulation testbeds.
pain_points: Standard causal discovery tools (e.g., conditional independence tests) do not scale computationally to high-dimensional spatial climate fields.
Ill-conditioning and non-invertibility of the lag-0 covariance matrix C(0) when the spatial dimension N exceeds or approaches sample size T.
Finite sample size and autocorrelation lead to spurious response functions in linear response theory.
Unobserved/hidden state variables can violate Markovianity assumptions when relying solely on SST fields.
Quasi-Gaussian assumption requires pre-processing (e.g., high-pass filtering or non-linear coordinate transforms) when applied to non-Gaussian climate fields.
extraction_notes: The study presents a two-stage diagnostic framework: (1) distance-constrained network community detection (Infomap) to reduce 31,141 grid points to 19 regional patterns, and (2) fluctuation-dissipation response theory with an analytical null model to quantify causal interbasin linkages.
